threepl.netlist.xilinx

Class XNetlistOptimise

  • java.lang.Object
    • threepl.netlist.xilinx.XNetlistOptimise

  • public class XNetlistOptimise
extends java.lang.Object
    This class contains static methods to optimise generic gates and family-specific components in the netlist. Many of these optimisations check for unconnected outputs and eliminate the element where found. These are probably unnecessary as the place-and-route will eliminate them anyway. I guess it makes for a shorter and neater netlist file.

        private static int optimisegates()

        public static void convertSelectors()

      • convertGenericToSpecific

        public static void convertGenericToSpecific()
        Convert generic elements to family-specific elements where necessary. Up until this point generic gates, AND, OR, XOR and XNOR, have an arbitrary number of inputs. These must be mapped into elements of maximum width available in the FPGA family.

      • optimiseMUXCY

        private static NetConstants.Ctype optimiseMUXCY(Element element)
        Check a MUXCY for output not connected, in which case remove it. Check for constant s input, in which case delete the MUXCY and connect the output net to the appropriate input net. Check for inputs CI and DI both constant, in which case output is HI, LO, S or !S. Check for input CI LO and DI connected to S, in which case output is LO.
        Parameters:
        element - is the MUXCY element
        Returns:
        code for unchanged, changed or stripped

      • optimiseMUXF

        private static NetConstants.Ctype optimiseMUXF(Element element)
        Check a MUXF5, MUXF6 etc for constant s input. If so delete the MUXF and connect the output net to the appropriate input net. Check for inputs I0 and I1 both constant, in which case output is HI, LO, S or !S.
        Parameters:
        element - is the MUXF element
        Returns:
        code for unchanged, changed or stripped

      • optimiseMULT_AND

        private static NetConstants.Ctype optimiseMULT_AND(Element element)
        Check a MULT_AND for an unconnected output and remove if so. If any inputs are GND, remove and connect output to GND. If any inputs are VCC, remove the input.
        Parameters:
        element - is a MULTAND element
        Returns:
        code for unchanged, changed or stripped

      • optimiseXORCY

        private static NetConstants.Ctype optimiseXORCY(Element element)
        Check an XORCY for an unconnected output and remove if so. If the CI input is GND, eliminate the XORCY and connect the output net to the LI input. If the CI input is VCC, strip the XORCY, change it to an INV and connect the LI input as input I and reconnect the output.
        Parameters:
        element - is the XORCY element
        Returns:
        code for unchanged, changed or stripped

      • optimiseOBUFFD

        private static void optimiseOBUFFD()
        Check for an FD whose output goes to an OBUF and also goes elsewhere. Replicate the FD for each OBUF plus one extra for all other sinks.

      • optimiseOBUFTFD

        private static void optimiseOBUFTFD()
        Check for an FD whose output goes to an OBUFT I input and also goes elsewhere. Replicate the FD for each OBUFT plus one extra for all other sinks. Check for an FD whose output goes to an OBUFT T input and also goes elsewhere. Replicate the FD for each OBUFT plus one extra for all other sinks. NOTE: ULTRASCALE I/O BLOCK DO NOT HAVE A T FLIPFLOP! IN THAT CASE SHOULD DUPICATE FD FOR EACH OBUFT BUT EACH WILL RESIDE IN A CLB. REMOVE IOB PROPERTY.

      • fdDuplicateInv

        private static Net fdDuplicateInv(Element e)
        Duplicate a flip-flop inverting its output. The D input of the old flip-flop will be inverted for the new flip-flop. An FDRSE is duplicated as an FDRSE with the R and S inputs swapped. An FDRE is duplicated as an FDSE with the old R input connected to the new S input and similarly an FDSE becomes an FDRE with S input connect to the new R input. The initial state is inverted via the INIT property.
        Parameters:
        e - is the flip-flop element to be duplicated
        Returns:
        the output signal of the new flip-flop
